fact: The Rw-CSIRT RFC 2350 profile states the National Cyber Security Authority was established by Law No 26/2017 of 31/05/2017 and hosts Rw-CSIRT as one of its divisions, with a constituency of all public and private institutions.

The NCSA page states Rw-CSIRT was established by the Rwanda Development Board in August 2014 and has operated under the National Cyber Security Authority since 15 December 2020, releasing alerts and advisories.
The National Cyber Security Authority is stated to have issued Application Software Security Directives on 16 April 2026, showing the body exists and operates.
ITWeb Africa reports the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) as an operating national body that made statements on the CyberHub centre of excellence opened on 2025-10-02.

The New Times states the National Cyber Security Authority and the Rwanda Computer Security Incident Response Team exist and are responsible for managing and responding to cybersecurity threats, and will be supported under the World Bank Digital Acceleration Project (USD 19.5 million for cybersecurity and data protection); article dated 2025-07-09 with the briefing on 7 July.

fact: Digital Policy Alert says Rwanda's National Cyber Security Authority was established in July 2017 and oversees data governance.
Digital Policy Alert says Rwanda launched its National Cybersecurity Strategy in August 2024, with seven objectives.

Connecting Africa reports that Rwanda's National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA), led by CEO David Kanamugire, signed partnerships with Airtel Rwanda and an MoU with MTN Rwanda on cybersecurity capacity.
